title: QUIC Non-HTTP/3 Interop-Testcase Inventory Architecture
purpose: Describe the canonical inventory/profile that records every documented non-HTTP/3 interop testcase as an explicit harness cell classification instead of collapsing the remaining cases into a generic unsupported fallthrough.
design_summary: The documented upstream QUIC testcase set is treated as a canonical inventory/profile, with each testcase assigned to one of four explicit classes: supported and executed, intentionally represented as unsupported with exit code 127, blocked by a named prerequisite, or not mappable through the current helper/workflow shape. The current helper-supported cells remain handshake, retry, transfer, and multiconnect, and the inventory/profile records versionnegotiation, keyupdate, and resumption as supported and executed while chacha20 remains prerequisite-blocked pending CipherSuitesPolicy support. Resumption is green only for the runner TLS session-resumption cell with managed SSLKEYLOGFILE export proof; HTTP/3, 0-RTT, anti-replay, and broader public API support remain out of scope. Zerortt remains prerequisite-blocked after the bounded internal early-data runtime proof because full hosted/Linux external runner success, client-side 0-RTT request-stream/packet-analysis proof, and harness classification have not promoted the cell; helper enumeration, resumption PSK acceptance, client 0-RTT probe emission, server-role dispatch, hosted workflow wiring, internal admission-gate proof, bounded server ZeroRtt delivery proof, and local first-flight X25519 proof do not make that cell green. The server-role harness path enables managed resumption tickets plus server early-data admission for runner-driven attempts, and the manual hosted workflow exposes an advisory `zerortt-server-proof` profile so Linux runner evidence can be captured beyond the 2026-05-09 local Windows long-filename setup blocker. Hosted run `25608915721` reached managed server execution and quic-go second-connection 0-RTT emission, but it also proved the former first-flight key-share/HelloRetryRequest incompatibility: the then-current P-256-only crypto floor sent HRR for quic-go's hybrid/X25519 offer, and quic-go treated that HRR as 0-RTT rejection. REQ-QUIC-CRT-0154 now locally proves bounded server first-flight X25519 acceptance for that captured offer. Hosted run `25617591021` confirmed the key-share/HRR blocker had moved forward but exposed a queued-final STREAM+FIN flush failure under transient congestion; commit `e7dece89` fixed that runtime path with focused RFC 9000 stream-send coverage. Hosted run `25617834482` then reached managed response/download success, but runner post-analysis still failed with `0-RTT size: 10618`, `1-RTT size: 16499`, and `Client sent too much data in 1-RTT packets.` The inventory/profile exists so the repository can work the remaining non-HTTP/3 cases down case-by-case without overclaiming support readiness or silently hiding them behind a generic unsupported fallback.
alternatives_considered: Keep the remaining non-HTTP/3 cases hidden behind a generic unsupported exit. Rejected because the request is to make the full suite visible as an explicit goal, not to bury it.
Treat the inventory/profile as a new protocol-support promise. Rejected because the slice is about explicit classification and evidence retention, not about turning every testcase green immediately.
edge_cases_and_constraints: HTTP/3 stays out of scope for this inventory/profile.
The inventory must distinguish supported cells from intentionally unsupported, prerequisite-blocked, and currently non-mappable cells.
A cell classified as unsupported must do so explicitly and honestly; it must not be implied by omission.
The inventory must not be read as a broad interop-readiness claim.
data_and_state_considerations: The inventory/profile is primarily static trace data plus per-cell dry-run or execution artifacts. It should remain separable from protocol runtime state and from the current supported-subset artifact bundles.
risks: The documented upstream testcase surface may drift if quic-interop-runner changes its QUIC docs.
Readers may mistake explicit inventory coverage for green support unless the classification labels stay prominent.
Some cases are blocked by runtime prerequisites outside the harness, so the profile must not collapse them into a generic unsupported bucket.

supplemental_sections.heading: Inventory Model
supplemental_sections.content: Current documented non-HTTP/3 cases include versionnegotiation, handshake, transfer, chacha20, keyupdate, retry, resumption, zerortt, multiconnect, v2, rebind-port, rebind-addr, and connectionmigration. The inventory/profile records the current class for each case, with versionnegotiation, keyupdate, and resumption now green while chacha20 remains blocked on the runner CipherSuitesPolicy prerequisite. Zerortt remains blocked until full hosted/Linux runner success, client-side 0-RTT request-stream/packet-analysis proof, and harness classification are complete. Hosted run `25617834482` reached managed response/download success after the prior X25519 and queued-final-stream fixes, but the runner still failed packet analysis because too much data used 1-RTT packets. The internal admission-gate proof under ARC-QUIC-CRT-0048, bounded internal early-data runtime proof under ARC-QUIC-CRT-0049, local X25519 proof under ARC-QUIC-CRT-0050, runtime queued-final-stream proof under the RFC 9000 stream-send home, and server-role runner dispatch are necessary but not support evidence by themselves. Resumption is limited to the checked runner TLS session-resumption cell with SSLKEYLOGFILE-backed proof. Cases can move from blocked or unsupported to executed as the underlying protocol slices land.
